items.followUp: Why is air considered a mixture while carbon dioxide is a compound?

rubric.why: Identifies a distinguishing property of the soft drink mixture.
rubric.description: States that a soft drink has variable composition or that its components retain their properties.
rubric.how: Award for either valid property of a mixture.

rubric.why: Shows that water is a compound formed from elements in a fixed proportion.
rubric.description: Identifies water as H₂O, or states that its elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
rubric.how: Award for the formula or the fixed-ratio chemical combination.

modelAnswer: A soft drink is a mixture because its components are physically mixed and its composition can vary.
Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio (H₂O).

items.followUp: Name the elements present in the second period of the Periodic Table.

rubric.why: Hydrogen is one of the two elements in the first period.
Helium is the other element in the first period.

modelAnswer: The elements in the first period are hydrogen and helium.

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the property on which the modern Periodic Table is based.

rubric.why: The law relates the periodic recurrence of properties to atomic number.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
rubric.how: Award both marks for the complete law; award one mark for correctly identifying atomic number as the basis.

modelAnswer: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: Name the groups present in the p-block of the Periodic Table.

rubric.why: Group 1 (IA) of the s-block is called the alkali metals.
rubric.description: Names the alkali metals (Group 1 or IA).
rubric.how: Award one mark for the correct name or group number.

rubric.why: Group 2 (IIA) of the s-block is called the alkaline earth metals.
rubric.description: Names the alkaline earth metals (Group 2 or IIA).
rubric.how: Award one mark for the correct name or group number.

modelAnswer: The s-block contains the alkali metals (Group 1 or IA) and the alkaline earth metals (Group 2 or IIA).

items.followUp: How do atoms form an ionic bond to attain a stable electronic configuration?

rubric.why: Atoms react to achieve a more stable outer-shell arrangement.
rubric.description: States that atoms react to attain a stable electronic configuration, like that of a noble gas.
rubric.how: Award one mark for the stability or noble-gas configuration idea.

rubric.why: Completing the valence shell explains how atoms attain that stability.
rubric.description: Mentions completing the outer shell or doing so by losing, gaining, or sharing electrons.
rubric.how: Award one mark for a valid completion mechanism.

modelAnswer: Atoms react with each other to attain a stable electronic configuration, usually by completing their outermost shell.
They do this by losing, gaining, or sharing electrons.

items.followUp: Define a polar covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: Equal sharing of the bonding electrons is the defining feature of a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a non-polar covalent bond as one in which the bonded atoms share electrons equally.
rubric.how: Award one mark for stating equal sharing of electrons.

rubric.why: These molecules contain non-polar covalent bonds between identical atoms.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example, such as H₂, Cl₂, O₂, or N₂.
rubric.how: Award one mark for any correct example.

modelAnswer: A non-polar covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the bonded atoms share the bonding electrons equally.
Examples include H₂, Cl₂, O₂, and N₂.

items.followUp: Define diffusion in liquids and give one example.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the spontaneous intermixing of particles due to their random motion.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion of gases as their spontaneous intermixing due to random motion of particles.
rubric.how: Award one mark for spontaneous intermixing or the random-motion explanation.

rubric.why: A familiar example demonstrates gas particles spreading through space.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example, such as the smell of perfume spreading through a room.
rubric.how: Award one mark for a valid example.

modelAnswer: Diffusion of gases is the spontaneous intermixing of gas particles due to their random motion, from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
For example, the smell of perfume spreads throughout a room.

items.followUp: Define an amorphous solid and give one example.

rubric.why: Crystalline solids have particles arranged in a regular, repeating pattern.
rubric.description: Defines a crystalline solid by the regular, orderly arrangement of its particles.
rubric.how: Award one mark for the regular arrangement or the related definite geometrical shape.

rubric.why: These are examples of crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as sodium chloride, sugar, or quartz.
rubric.how: Award one mark for any suitable example.

modelAnswer: A crystalline solid is a solid whose particles are arranged in a regular, orderly pattern, giving it a definite geometrical shape.
Examples include sodium chloride (NaCl), sugar, and quartz.
